reader.notes: Re-read on this branch (kb/Work PB2724): '[IS] GLOBAL' is now ONE grammar rule, globalClause, referenced by the data description, file description and report description entries (and the 2002 constant and screen entries); the deleted fileGlobalExternalClause and reportGlobalClause were its FD and RD copies. VisitGlobalClause gates the Linkage form only when its parent is a dataDescriptionClause, so the edition decision is unchanged for 85 source.

refuter.evidence: Code read independently at the pin, starting from the grammar: `git grep -i globalexternalclause\|reportglobalclause -- src` finds only a historical comment in DiagnosticCatalog.cs, so no reader of the deleted rules survives; fileDescriptionClause, reportDescriptionClause, dataDescriptionClause and constantEntryBody reference the one globalClause, and fileDescriptionClause and dataDescriptionClause the one externalClause. Every consumer of the FD's attributes reads FileModel.IsExternal/IsGlobal (set only in BindFileSection's two arms) or ReportModel.IsGlobal (set only in BindReportDescriptionClauses); OoDefinitionRules.GlobalClauseSites lists the five hosts. The only edition reads on the path are VisitExternalizedNamePhrase (AS, 2002) and VisitGlobalClause, now restricted to a dataDescriptionClause parent in the Linkage Section, which no FD or RD can be. Attacks past the reader's probes at --std 85: x4_dd_bad.cob refuses 'GLOBAL IS GLOBAL' on a 01 (COBOL2423) and 'EXTERNAL AS' on a 01 (COBOL0900); x5_same_area.cob refuses SAME RECORD AREA over a GLOBAL FD (COBOL2738, SR3); x1_fd_formats.cob and x2_rd_code.cob admit the FD and RD forms with and without IS. The narrowed VisitGlobalClause test (parent is dataDescriptionClause) cannot let an 85 Linkage GLOBAL through: in 85 source the only host of globalClause under the Linkage Section is a data description entry (no constant entry or screen section exists at 85), and r6_global_bad still prints COBOL0900 for it.
